title: p0001
universal_lens: Presentation bias constitutes a structural observational selection effect. Mathematically, it manifests as a non-stationary confounding variable in the likelihood function of user interactions. Correcting for this requires an inverse probability weighting operator that decouples the intrinsic relevance of an entity from its positional exposure.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, implicit user feedback maps to fan engagement metrics (e.g., click-through rates on athlete profiles). The presentation bias model acts as a Bayesian prior adjustment, correcting for the 'home-field' or 'prime-time' exposure advantage, ensuring inferred true talent distributions remain conformally calibrated against raw interaction data.
gse_mapping: For GSE, search result ranking isomorphic to situational state transitions. A team's tactical choice (state) receives implicit feedback based on game context. The bias model adjusts transition probabilities by accounting for contextual leverage, isolating the true efficacy of a play from the mere opportunity presented by the game clock.

primitives.name: Positional Bias Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Jan. 20, 2015 (54) MODIFYING SEARCH RESULT RANKING BASED ON IMPLICIT USER FEEDBACK AND A MODEL
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p: Probability of exposure (dimensionless), i: Position index (integer)
primitives.assumptions: The probability of a user interacting with an item due solely to its position is stationary over the observation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities arise if the estimated exposure probability approaches zero, causing infinite variance in the inverse probability weights.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's adjustment for situational leverage; normalizing the success rate of a play call by the baseline probability of that situation occurring.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of click-through rates across different UI positions before and after bias correction.

primitives.name: Bias-Corrected Ranking Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: BIAS (75) Inventors: Hyung-Jin Kim, Sunnyvale, CA (US); Adrian D. Corduneanu, Mountain View, CA (US) (73)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: Adjusted relevance score (dimensionless), w: Inverse bias weight (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: The underlying relevance metric is linearly separable from the presentation bias factor in the high-dimensional feature space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under severe collinearity where top-ranked items are inherently the most relevant, making it impossible to disentangle position from quality.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's TrueSkill adjustments, stripping away the inflation caused by media coverage frequency to reveal core athletic performance.
layer2.telemetry: Rank correlation (Kendall's tau) between bias-corrected scores and long-term empirical win rates.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical derivation begins by modeling the user's interaction as a stochastic process governed by two competing potentials: intrinsic relevance and positional salience. Let $y_{ij}$ be the binary outcome of user $u$ clicking document $d$ at rank $j$. The standard assumption in information retrieval is that $P(y_{ij}=1)$ depends solely on the relevance $r_{id}$. However, the patent introduces a confounding variable: the presentation bias $b_j$, representing the a priori probability of a click at rank $j$ regardless of content. To isolate the true relevance signal, we construct a joint likelihood function $L = \prod P(y_{ij} | r_{id}, b_j)$. By applying an Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, we iteratively estimate the latent relevance scores while simultaneously updating the bias parameters $b_j$. This creates a dual optimization landscape where the gradient descent on relevance is orthogonalized against the gradient of the positional bias. The resulting operator acts as a high-pass filter, removing low-frequency trends associated with UI layout and exposing the high-frequency signal of genuine user preference. In the context of sports intelligence, this mirrors the necessity of separating a player's fundamental ability from the artificial inflation caused by being featured in prime-time broadcasts or starting lineups. The failure mode occurs when the bias matrix becomes singular, typically when the system enters an echo chamber where only highly biased items are ever presented, collapsing the observability of the true relevance distribution.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to the foundational work in causal inference, specifically the back-door criterion established by Judea Pearl. Historically, it also connects to the Bradley-Terry models used in early Elo rating systems, which implicitly assumed that match outcomes were purely functions of skill, ignoring home-field advantages. The explicit modeling of presentation bias represents a maturation of these probabilistic frameworks, incorporating structural confounders previously treated as irreducible noise in psychometric and econometric analyses.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the decision actor here requires understanding the cognitive heuristics of the user. The user is not a rational optimizer maximizing information gain; rather, they are a bounded rational agent heavily influenced by visual hierarchy and proximity. The 'mind' of the user assumes that top-ranked items are endorsed by the system, creating a self-fulfilling prophecy of engagement. The opposing agent—the ranking algorithm—must anticipate this cognitive shortcut. It must act as a counter-factual reasoner, asking: 'Would this user have engaged with this entity if it had been placed at the bottom of the list?' This adversarial dynamic between user heuristic and algorithmic correction forms the core of the theory of mind.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises when the presentation bias becomes perfectly collinear with the true relevance metric. If the system consistently places the objectively best items at the top, the bias estimator cannot distinguish between 'clicks due to position' and 'clicks due to quality.' In such regimes, the inverse probability weights explode, introducing massive variance into the relevance estimates. Furthermore, if the user population shifts demographics rapidly, the stationary assumption of the bias model breaks, leading to leakage where historical positional preferences contaminate current relevance assessments. The cross-layer veto mandates halting updates when the condition number of the exposure matrix exceeds a predefined threshold.
